model_claims.text: With length_sort=True and sort_order="native", imports are not ordered by length; longer imports appear before shorter ones when name lengths cross a digit boundary.
model_claims.source_quote: With `length_sort=True` and `sort_order="native"`, imports are no longer ordered by length:

model_claims.text: Zero-padding the embedded length to six digits makes lexicographic key order match numeric length order under plain sorted() while preserving natural sort behavior.
model_claims.source_quote: Zero-pad the embedded length to a fixed width of six digits in both `module_key` and `section_key`, so lexicographic key order equals numeric length order under plain `sorted()` while `naturally()` keeps producing identical keys after `int()` strips the zeros:

model_claims.text: Key generation micro-benchmark shows parity between old and new implementations (225.7 ms vs 215.2 ms per run).
model_claims.source_quote: - Key generation micro-benchmark (verbatim copy of the old `module_key` vs the new one, same process, 200 reps x 9, best-of, 1000 module names, Windows / CPython 3.11): old 225.7 ms vs new 215.2 ms per run - parity (within run-to-run noise).

model_claims.text: Full pipeline benchmark shows parity between main and patched versions (~700 ms vs ~703 ms).
model_claims.source_quote: - Full pipeline with the review benchmark from #2703 (`isort.code` of 1000 generated imports, `length_sort=True, sort_order="native"`, `number=30, repeat=7`, best-of, median of 3 runs): main ~700 ms vs patched ~703 ms - parity.

model_claims.text: The unit test test_length_sort_native_order_issue_2698 covers various scenarios and fails on main but passes with the patch.
model_claims.source_quote: `tests/unit/test_isort.py::test_length_sort_native_order_issue_2698` covers straight imports, `reverse_sort`, `force_sort_within_sections` (the `section_key` path), `length_sort_straight`, and from-import member names at a digit boundary (lengths 1, 8, 10). Red on `main`, green with this patch.

model_rejected_claims.text: Differential testing shows 2120 cases unchanged and 400 cases changed only when both sort_order="native" and a length flag are used, with patched output in nondecreasing import-name length order.
model_rejected_claims.source_quote: - A differential run over 120 deterministic 3-module import blocks and from-import blocks crossed with 20 option sets (2520 cases) against `main@5d9c9619`: - 2120 cases byte-identical (every case without both `sort_order="native"` and a length flag). - 400 changed cases, all 400 confined to option sets containing both `sort_order="native"` and `length_sort` / `length_sort_straight` / `length_sort_sections` - exactly the intended scope, with the patched output in nondecreasing import-name length order.
